notes: Two follow-ups to peer-cohorts, both from the same realisation: if a peer group is a cohort, it should behave like one everywhere. It now enters the price decomposition. A name's own peer group joins its sector, size and indexes as a cohort the decomposition measures it against — so "cheap vs peers" and "cheap vs the sector" become two reported facts with the spread between them shown as robustness. Because a curated peer set is not a sample of a broad population but the comparison universe itself, it clears a lower eligibility floor (6, versus 12 for a broad median) — the number a comps table
